acceptance_criteria.criterion: '{if contains: $VAR "term"}' translates to '{% if "term" in var %}'
Case-insensitive variant adds '|lower' to variable and lowercases the term
Multiple terms joined with 'or' for contains, 'and' for not-contains
'{if not-contains: $VAR "term"}' translates to '{% if "term" not in var %}'
List-contains subtypes return the not-implemented stub
Both {if} and {elseif} variants produce correct output via shared AbstractIfBase

summary: Implemented _translateContains() in HubL AbstractIfBase with contains/not-contains logic, case-insensitive support, multi-term OR/AND joining, and list-* stub passthrough.
Added IfContainsTests.php covering if and elseif variants, all 6 acceptance criteria verified.
Full test suite (309 tests) and PHPStan level 9 pass with zero new violations.

comments.note: AbstractIfBase._translateContains() and _translateSearch(): the $caseSensitive parameter is misnamed — it carries the isCaseInsensitive() value (true = case-insensitive). Both HubL and Velocity share this quirk. Renaming to $caseInsensitive in both translators would prevent confusion every time this method is touched.

summary: All six acceptance criteria are met.
Implementation is correct, idiomatic, and PHPStan-clean at level 9.
No blocking issues found. Three low-priority non-blocking suggestions recorded as comments.

comments.note: Signature parity with Velocity AbstractIfBase is exact — same parameter order and names. $regexEnabled is silently ignored, which is correct since HubL's 'in' operator has no regex variant. A one-line inline comment ('// Regex has no HubL equivalent — ignored.') would prevent future confusion but is non-blocking.

$caseSensitive parameter is semantically inverted (carries isCaseInsensitive()). The inline comment already documents this quirk, but a follow-up rename to $caseInsensitive across both HubL and Velocity AbstractIfBase would eliminate the persistent mental inversion tax for future maintainers. Non-blocking; recommend a dedicated cleanup ticket.

Empty $searchTerms produces implode() of an empty array, yielding '{% if  %}' — malformed HubL. Upstream factory validation prevents this path today. Adding an early-return guard ('if(empty($searchTerms)) return "";') would harden the method against future callers and make the contract explicit. Non-blocking.

Test coverage is complete for all stated ACs. No test for empty $searchTerms edge case (consistent with QA note). No test for regex=true on non-list contains (silently ignored, acceptable). The HubLTestCase + runCommands() pattern is used correctly throughout.
